# We Shall Build

> Through five client engagements (a build-vs-buy call made under timeline pressure for a regulated lender, BlueMoney; a founder learning to evaluate technical hires, PowerMarket; through-the-door delivery with clear documentation in a complex and ambiguous environment, Ourish; a long-term partnership refining a banking-grade email platform, Sable International; and an AI-built prototype taken safely from demo to production by deciding which AI-generated decisions survive, BauAI), one thread runs consistently: senior architectural judgement bringing engineering discipline and rigour to increasingly AI-generated codebases. What to keep, what to cut, and what will hold up in production.
>
> AI can build it fast. That's the problem.
>
> For founders and technical leads facing the decisions whose consequences are paid in time and money: build or buy, who to hire, and whether what AI built will hold. I've been making those decisions in production for twenty years.

Productised senior-architect engagements that start small and lead to embedded work. You don't make the wrong decision, the wrong hire, or the wrong bet on production. It usually starts with a free fifteen-minute conversation to work out whether it's worth a longer one. The site features deep-dive technical articles, the ten We shall commandments, and a four-rung engagement ladder, all visible at once.

## Key pages

- [Home](https://weshall.build/): Landing page with brand positioning, engagement story cards, and service overview
- [About](https://weshall.build/en/about/): From Lehman Brothers through Inbotiqa co-founder to independent consulting
- [Services](https://weshall.build/en/services/): It starts with a conversation: a fifteen-minute call to meet, then an honest hour, a short working sprint, or ongoing monthly advisory, as far as the problem needs
- [Blog](https://weshall.build/en/blog/): Deep-dive technical analysis, operational case studies, and engineering philosophy
- [Contact](https://weshall.build/en/contact/): "Reach out." Primary path: Let's talk, a free fifteen-minute conversation with a founder-engineer, via Calendly, no pitch, no obligation. Second door: the honest hour, booked via Upwork. Writing-first is tertiary: a LinkedIn link lives in the site footer.
